column1: # Language codes with no living speech community. A name whose EVERY source tag is one
# of these leaves the row it is on. See build_library.drop_dead_language_names.
# ⚠️ WHY THIS EXISTS. 'flour' was measured at 16 members and 10 of them were Middle
#    English spellings: fflour, fflowr, fleur, floure, flowr, flowre, flowyr, flor, flur,
#    floor. Nobody writes a recipe in Middle English, so every holder in the library was
#    showing more members than it has. This is a FILTER, not a judgement about a name.
# ⚠️ LATIN IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, AND IT IS THE LARGEST DEAD LANGUAGE IN THE STORE at
#    3,420 name rows. The binomial flag rests entirely on the Latin tag: 56 rows carry
#    the flag and all 56 have a Latin tag on the canonical, so cutting 'la' would not
#    weaken that flag, it would stop it. Shape alone was wrong about 9 names in 10 and
#    fired on 705 rows, and the Latin tag is what cut it to 56. Latin is excluded from
#    MEMBER COUNTING instead, where a binomial is not a name a cook writes.
# ⚠️ LIVING LANGUAGES ARE NOT IN THIS FILE AND ARE A DIFFERENT ACT. English Wiktionary
#    spans 1,588 languages, most of them living and obscure, and voanjo in Malagasy and
#    asukar in Cebuano are real ingredient names. The library exists to recognize what
#    anyone imports, so a Tagalog or Amharic name has a claim that fflowr does not.
# ⚠️ TWO CODES WERE MISCLASSIFIED BY HAND AND CAUGHT BEFORE COUNTING. 'zom' is Zou and
#    'sxu' is Upper Saxon. Both are living and neither is here.
# HOW THE LIST WAS BUILT. Every distinct lang in join.db, named from the top-level
# 'lang' field of a wiktextract entry carrying that lang_code, then classified three
# ways: a name beginning Old, Middle, Ancient, Classical, Early Modern, Primitive, Koine
# or Vulgar; a code containing '-pro', which is Wiktionary's reconstructed proto-language
# marker; or a hand-named ancient language with no modern descendant in use.
# ⚠️ READ THE FIRST 'lang' KEY WITH A REGEX AND IT COMES OUT WRONG. The raw entry JSON
#    nests a 'lang' inside every translation block, so a regex returned Sranan Tongo for
